title: Many rooms (John 14:1–7)
hook: let not your heart be troubled; in my Father's house are many rooms
carry: let not your heart be troubled

segments.voice: Yesterday, a new commandment: love one another as I have loved you, the sentence behind Maundy Thursday, and Tertullian's words about it: see how they love one another. Your line was by this, all will know. What visible love did you show? Day six hundred thirty-one.

Some houses keep a room ready. The bed made up. A towel on the end of it. Someone thought of the guest before the guest arrived. Now go back to that supper table. Judas has gone. Jesus has just told Peter he'll deny him. He's said he's leaving, and they can't come yet. The room is full of fear. Their whole lives have been built around following this man for years. And the first thing he says to them is about their hearts.

"Let not your heart be troubled: ye believe in God, believe also in me." Remember, a few days ago Jesus himself said, now is my soul troubled. He knows the feeling from inside. He isn't scolding them for being afraid. He's giving them somewhere to put the fear. Then: "In my Father's house are many mansions: if it were not so, I would have told you. I go to prepare a place for you." Mansions sounds like big estates on a hill. But in the English of the King James Bible, a mansion simply meant a dwelling place, somewhere you stay. The Greek word is monē, from a verb meaning to remain, to abide. That same verb will be all over the next chapter: abide in me. So the picture isn't a gated community. It's a big family house with room for everyone, a place to stay and not have to leave. And many rooms: no shortage, no waiting list. And Jesus goes ahead to get them ready, like someone making up the bed before a guest arrives. Thomas says it plainly: "Lord, we know not whither thou goest; and how can we know the way?" And Jesus answers: "I am the way, the truth, and the life: no man cometh unto the Father, but by me." Christians hold this line at the center of their faith in Jesus. Churches have long talked about what it means for people of other paths, and they don't all answer it the same way. For Thomas, at that table, it meant: you don't need a map. You need me.
screen: `THOMAS: HOW CAN WE KNOW THE WAY?`
then, large: `LET NOT YOUR HEART BE TROUBLED.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: prepare a room or a bed for a guest. If you can, get up and tidy a corner, a couch, a chair where someone could sit. If you can't move right now, picture a room in your home. Settle, and breathe. Imagine who might come: a friend, a relative, a stranger who needs somewhere to stay. Picture making it ready. Clean sheets, a glass of water, a light left on. Think of the care that goes into a room prepared ahead. If you pray, you can give thanks for a place made ready for you. If you don't, simply enjoy the thought of welcoming someone. The bell holds the time.
Many rooms. Jesus's promise at the supper: in my Father's house are many dwelling places, and he goes ahead to prepare one.
Your line: let not your heart be troubled. Today, when worry rises, say the line once, and then make one small space ready for someone else. Day six hundred thirty-one.

howItsDone: Christians often read these words at funerals and memorial services, and some also pray "let not your heart be troubled" in times of worry.

original.note: Greek: a dwelling, a place to stay. From menō, to remain or abide.

trapdoor: what you thought: heaven has mansions, like big houses on a hill.
what it means: a big family house with room for everyone, and Jesus going ahead to make it ready.
what a scholar hears: monai, dwelling places, comes from menō, abide, the word that runs all through John 15; "mansions" meant dwellings in King James English.
recall: went out to meet him on the road

notes: 'Mansion' in early modern English = dwelling place (from Latin mansio, via the Vulgate 'mansiones multae'). Confirm.
μονή from μένω (abide), used heavily in John 15. Confirm.

John 14:6 handled descriptively: central to Christian faith; churches differ on implications for people of other faiths (exclusivist, inclusivist and other views). No ranking. Keeper should confirm this balance.

'Three years' of ministry (John mentions three Passovers) is a traditional count, not settled; voice softened in review to 'for years'. Fork option quote of 14:5 restored to exact KJV wording ('and how can we know the way?').
Index title 'Many rooms'; KJV 'many mansions'. The script explains both.
